desk.headline: Revenue up 12% to $4.94bn and adjusted EPS up 24% to $9.39, both beats; full-year outlook raised but Q4 profit guide below estimates
results: Revenue rose 12% to $4.94bn and gross bookings 11% to $34.0bn, both above the company's own guidance.
The B2B arm (travel sold through partners such as airlines and banks) again led: bookings +19%, revenue +23%. Consumer brands grew revenue 6%.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 17% to $1.69bn with the margin up 1.35 points to 34.2%, helped by more efficient consumer marketing; B2B margin slipped 1.3 points to 27.5%.
Adjusted EPS jumped 24% to $9.39 (GAAP $8.42, +15%), boosted by a smaller share count.
Bought back about 2m shares for $576m in the quarter and declared a $0.48 quarterly dividend.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 targets for bookings, revenue and margin expansion were all lifted. The first Q4 outlook implies slower growth: revenue up 4–6% and adjusted EBITDA of $830–880m, which coverage says is below what analysts expected.

points: Management said B2B partners ran heavy marketing and growth was double-digit in every region; the 2025 CarTrawler deal and new partner tools broaden the platform.
Q4 caution was put down to the US election cycle, travel disruption in Europe and the Middle East, and tougher B2B comparisons.
The CFO signalled that marketing savings will be smaller from here after a year of big efficiency gains; recent acquisitions and investment also weigh on margins.
Expedia is deepening links with AI assistants such as Google's AI Mode and Meta's Muse; traffic from them is still small and the economics are not yet settled.
CEO Ariane Gorin pointed to record package attach rates and wider use of AI internally to cut costs.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks Equity Research and StockStory, 5 Nov 2026; earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2)

watch: Whether Q4 bookings growth slows to the guided 3–5% or holds up better.
B2B margins as partner mix and acquisitions weigh.
How much travel demand flows through AI assistants, and on what commercial terms.
